channel.title: Press Releases on U.S. Department of the Treasury
channel.description: The Department of the Treasury manages federal finances, collects taxes and duties, enforces finance and tax laws, and protects the nation's financial systems.

item.title: Remarks from Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent at the National Committee on U.S.-China Relations Gala
item.description:
As prepared for delivery. 

Thank you, Evan [Greenberg], for that introduction, and for the invitation to be here. It gives me great pleasure to join you on this occasion.

More than as representatives of the world’s largest economies, we meet tonight as stewards of one of this century’s most consequential relationships.

Of course, when this Committee was formed in 1966, the Pacific was only the most visible distance between the United States and China. Formal diplomatic ties were still over a decade away. Our governments rarely spoke. And our people, likewise, rarely met.

item.title: FATF Recognizes Effectiveness of U.S. AML/CFT System, Advances Key Illicit Finance Initiatives
item.description:
PARIS—Last week, senior Treasury officials led a U.S. government delegation to the Financial Action Task Force’s(FATF) plenary meetings.  The FATF, the global standard-setting body for countering money laundering, terror financing, and proliferation financing, concluded its first Plenary under the United Kingdom presidency.  The FATF adopted the Mutual Evaluation Reports of the United States and Mexico, reiterated the call to impose countermeasures on Iran, agreed to publish a new report on scam centers, and agreed to accelerate global implementation of digital asset-related standards. 

STOPPING IRANIAN ILLICIT FINANCE

Iran remains on the FATF’s blacklist, and the FATF called upon all nations to implement reimposed United Nations Security Council Resolutions related to Iran’s ongoing lack of compliance with its nuclear agreements. The FATF also reminded all jurisdictions to impose countermeasures on Iran to restrict correspondent banking, digital asset transactions, and business relationships with Iran.

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Sanctions Eight Canadian Money Services Businesses Enabling Iranian Regime
item.description:
Several of the Targets Also Worked with Narcotrafficker and Former Olympic Snowboarder Ryan Wedding

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated eight money services businesses based in Canada that enable the Iranian regime, sanctioned entities associated with the regime, and other illicit actors that move assets into and out of Iran.  These companies facilitate the exchange of Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets to enable international transactions involving Iran.  Many of these businesses have facilitated transactions with sanctioned Iranian digital asset exchanges, as well as with digital asset addresses associated with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Severs MEXC Global’s Access to the U.S. Financial System
item.description:
CVC Exchanger Facilitated at Least $16 Billion in Illicit Finance, Including for IRGC-Qods Force

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued an order effectively cutting off MEXC Global’s access to the U.S. financial system. MEXC Global is a convertible virtual currency (CVC) exchanger that has facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions connected to Iranian, North Korean, and Russian sanctions evasion, as well as cybercrime, including by transacting directly with sanctioned actors.

item.title: READOUT: Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent’s Call with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng
item.description:
WASHINGTON— Today, Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent and United States Trade Representative Jameison Greer spoke with Vice Premier He Lifeng of the People’s Republic of China to discuss the bilateral economic relationship and implementation of the Busan arrangement. The two officials reaffirmed the value of maintaining direct and candid communication.

Secretary Bessent emphasized the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments made in Busan and raised concerns about recent Chinese actions. He underscored that continued progress depends on concrete results and that the United States will closely assess China’s implementation of the arrangement.

item.title: Treasury Targets Global Scam Networks and the Corporate Infrastructure That Enables Them
item.description:
WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned four individuals and 41 entities that support the business network of Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization (TCO) previously sanctioned by the United States for its role in cyber-enabled fraud, money laundering, and human trafficking.  Additionally, OFAC designated a Malaysian individual who defrauded U.S. victims by managing a network of Africa-based scammers.

“Cyber scam syndicates continue to steal billions of dollars from American victims while relying on sophisticated international business networks to launder their illicit proceeds,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent. “Treasury remains committed to dismantling every layer of these organizations—from their leadership to the corporate structures and financial facilitators that enable them to operate with impunity.”

item.title: Treasury, IRS Announce Opportunity Zones Designations for Over 6,500 Communities Across America
item.description:
The Working Families Tax Cuts Created a Permanent Process for States to Direct More Capital to Overlooked Communities 

WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today announced the Qualified Opportunity Zone (QOZ) designations for all 50 states, territories, and the District of Columbia.  

Under President Trump’s Working Families Tax Cuts, the Opportunity Zone tax incentive was permanently renewed, enhanced incentives for investment in eligible rural communities were added, and a process was established for redesignating zones every ten years. The new QOZ designations will become effective on January 1, 2027, and retain this designation for ten years.

item.title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Global Maritime Fraud Network Supporting Iranian Regime
item.description:
Network Circumvented Maritime Law to Enable Iran’s Shadow Fleet

WASHINGTON—Today, as part of Operation Economic Outcast, the U.S. Department of the Treasury targeted the vast criminal network of India-based Suniel Kumar Sharma and his spouse, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, who have supported Iran’s shadow fleet through a web maritime fraud. Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies.

item.title: Quarterly Refunding Statement of Assistant Secretary for Financial Markets Hunter McMaster
item.description:
WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury is offering $125 billion of Treasury securities to refund approximately $97 billion of privately-held Treasury notes and bonds maturing on November 15, 2026.  This issuance will raise new cash from private investors of approximately $28 billion.  The securities are:

  • A 3-year note in the amount of $58 billion, maturing November 15, 2029;
  • A 10-year note in the amount of $42 billion, maturing November 15, 2036;
  • A 30-year bond in the amount of $25 billion, maturing November 15, 2056.

The 3-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Monday, November 9, 2026.  The 10-year note will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.  The 30-year bond will be auctioned at 1:00 p.m. ET on Thursday, November 12, 2026.  All these auctions will take place on a yield basis and will settle on Monday, November 16, 2026.

item.title: Report to the Secretary of the Treasury from the Treasury Borrowing Advisory Committee
item.description:
Dear Mr. Secretary,

Since the TBAC last met in early August, Treasury markets have repriced toward a higher path for interest rates, reflecting stronger economic activity and associated financing needs, persistent energy-supply disruptions, and the Federal Reserve’s initial rate hike and projections for further increases. The selloff in rates was led by the front end of the yield curve, with two-year yields rising by roughly 50bps and ten-year yields by roughly 40bps. The move accelerated in September and early October, with ten-year yields peaking around 5.4% and thirty-year yields around 5.7% in early October. Some of that increase has since reversed.
